newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed lower on Thursday, but fall was not dramatic as bund futures slowly started to recover in the afternoon.
Dealers said that business was mainly futures driven.
Greenspan's remarks on a possible rise in interest rates in the U.S. next week did not have much effect on guilder bonds.
"The market was mainly watching the Bund futures and they started to recover in the afternoon," said one dealer.
The June Bund future contract, lingering at 99.65 before Greenspan gave his testimony, were trading at 99.81 at 1720 GMT. The contracts hit a low of 99.52 in early trade.
The yield gap with Germany narrowed a little today, bringing the gap in the 10-year segment back to familiar levels.
The February 2007 bond slipped 0.29 to 99.35/43 today, yielding 4.92 percent or 0.11 basis points below the German equivalent.
Dealers said business had been somewhat nervous ahead of the announcement of a new Dutch special advances pact at 1500 GMT.
Some dealers feared a rise of 10 basis points for the special advances as result of the current guilder/mark rate, but the central bank left the rate unchanged at 2.90 percent.
